# Career Compass five-minute presentation draft

Update this script to match the actual hosted system before presenting on November 5. Do not call the local URL an online deployment.

## 0:00–0:40 Student need
Explain how students struggle to translate coursework and experience into evidence for a target job. State the chosen scope: resume coaching, skill planning and interview preparation alongside campus career services.

## 0:40–1:45 Demonstration
Use the fictional resume and target internship. Show a comparison, an uncertain requirement and the source text. Ask for a truthful resume improvement and a plan with a five-hour weekly budget. Distinguish a missing resume mention from a confirmed skill gap.

## 1:45–2:40 Agent and AI coding
Explain the browser → Node backend → OpenAI Responses API → bounded single-agent tools architecture. Open Sources and agent activity and show actual comparison or planning tool selection. Explain what Codex helped implement and the design decisions the group reviewed. There is one agent; multiple agents are unnecessary for the selected scope.

## 2:40–3:25 RAG
Show a generated answer and its retrieved guidance. Explain passage IDs/provenance, BM25, model generation, and source-ID validation. Check manually that a passage supports the advice. The library contains stored summaries and authored frameworks, not live web search.

## 3:25–4:10 Interview and evaluation
Ask for a tell-me-about-yourself draft, then supply fictional details and ask for a shorter version. Show the difference between drafting and explicitly requesting a mock interview. Report 83 automated tests and the small synthetic live checks honestly. The 22 comparison regression cases were used during development and are not a general-accuracy benchmark.

## 4:10–5:00 Privacy and limitations
Explain the server-side key, transmitted student context, source limitations, fact checking and redacted demonstration data. Show the actual hosted URL and instructor access only after deployment is complete. Report actual student feedback if collected; otherwise state that usefulness remains unvalidated. Summarize remaining limitations without claiming verified proficiency or hiring outcomes.
